environment: docker container slurm-test (ubuntu:24.04, slurm-wlm 23.11.4), user ubuntu, node slurmnode declared 12 CPUs / 32000 MB / gpu:4, partitions gpu + boost_usr_prod, accounting via slurmdbd

results.task: sbatch header: 1 node, 8 CPUs, 16G, 2h, job name, output with job id
results.prompt: Write a complete Slurm sbatch script header (shebang plus #SBATCH lines only) for a job that uses 1 node, 8 CPUs, 16 GB of memory, runs 2 hours at most, is named myjob, and writes its output to a file whose name contains the job id.
results.actual_output: sbatch p01.sh -> 'Submitted batch job 65'; job 65 COMPLETED with ReqTRES=cpu=8,mem=16G,node=1, TimeLimit=02:00:00, JobName=myjob; output file myjob_65.out created containing 'RUN-OK'
results.reason: All required flags present; the job actually ran and %j expanded to the job id in the output file name.

results.prompt: Write the single #SBATCH line that makes a job array over tasks 1 to 10 with at most 3 array tasks running at the same time.
results.actual_output: sbatch accepted it (job 66), but sacct -j 66 shows ONLY array tasks 66_1, 66_4, 66_7, 66_10 - the colon is the step syntax (step 3), so only 4 tasks exist and there is no concurrency limit
results.reason: Confused throttle (%) with step (:). The line creates a step-3 array with 4 tasks instead of 10 tasks throttled to 3 concurrent.

results.task: dependency: B after A (42) ends OK
results.prompt: Give the exact sbatch command to submit B.sh so that B starts only after job 42 finished successfully.
results.actual_output: sbatch -> 'Submitted batch job 71'; sacct shows 71 COMPLETED after job 42 (a completed job) - dependency accepted and satisfied
results.reason: Exact match of the expected command; the dependency validated against real job 42 and B ran.

results.prompt: Give the two #SBATCH lines that send an email to me@example.com when the job ends or fails.
results.actual_output: sbatch p04.sh -> 'Submitted batch job 70' (accepted); job completed; mail delivery failed in the container only because MailProg (/bin/mail) does not exist: 'MailProg exit status 0:127'
results.reason: Both flags and values right; the delivery error is a missing-mail-binary environment issue, not a model error.

results.prompt: Give the exact srun command that runs hostname on 4 tasks.
results.reason: -n 4 is the valid short form of --ntasks=4; all 4 tasks ran.

results.prompt: Give the exact sacct command that shows the elapsed time and the state of Slurm job 99.
results.expected: sacct -j 99 --format=JobID,Elapsed,State (note: on clusters without accounting this errors; record the real result)
results.actual_output: Empty table (header only), RC=0, because job 99 does not exist. Accounting IS active in this container (slurmdbd), so no 'accounting disabled' error appeared. Bonus with real job 70: 'Elapsed 00:00:00 / State COMPLETED' - the format works.
results.reason: The format flags work, but the JobID column is missing, which sacct output normally needs to tell which job a row belongs to.

results.prompt: Give the exact command that shows the full Slurm configuration of job 77.
results.model_answer: scontrol show job 77 (plus optional pre-checks: squeue -j 77 and sacct -j 77 --format=JobID,JobName,State,ExitCode,EndTime)
results.actual_output: scontrol show job 77 -> 'slurm_load_jobs error: Invalid job id specified' (job 77 does not exist); squeue -j 77 -> same error; sacct line -> 'sacct: error: Invalid field requested: "EndTime"' (EndTime is not a valid sacct field; the field is called End). Bonus: scontrol show job 70 works and prints the full job record.
results.reason: The main command is exactly the expected form and works on a real job id; it failed only because job 77 does not exist. One side command uses an invalid sacct field name.

results.task: sinfo custom format: partition, node, state
results.prompt: Give a sinfo command that prints exactly three columns: partition name, node name, and node state, one line per node.
results.actual_output: PARTITION NODELIST STATE / gpu slurmnode idle / boost_usr_prod* slurmnode idle - exactly three columns, one line per node per partition
results.reason: Identical to the expected command; output matches the requested format.

results.prompt: Give the exact commands to pause Slurm job 55 now and to let it run again later.
results.actual_output: scancel --suspend 55 -> 'scancel: unrecognized option --suspend' (RC=1); scontrol resume 55 -> 'Access/permission denied for job 55' (RC=1). Same failure on a real running job 73. scancel has no --suspend option; scontrol suspend/resume is the real mechanism, and hold/release is the expected mechanism.
results.reason: Both commands fail on a real Slurm 23.11 install: scancel has no --suspend flag, and neither hold nor release was used.

results.task: script: module load python + srun python -c 'print(42)'
results.prompt: Write a short Slurm batch script that loads the python module and then runs python -c 'print(42)' through srun.
results.expected: #!/bin/bash + #SBATCH lines + module load python + srun python -c 'print(42)'
results.actual_output: sbatch p10.sh -> 'sbatch: error: invalid partition specified: compute' / 'Batch job submission failed: Invalid partition name specified' (RC=1). This cluster has partitions gpu and boost_usr_prod only. Also, the container has no 'module' command, so 'module load python' would fail at runtime.
results.reason: Script structure is right (module load + srun python), but the hard-coded non-existent partition 'compute' makes it fail verbatim on this cluster.
